allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Two kids find themselves in the centre of a deadly game of cat and mouse after taking a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride.

facts.overview: Two kids find themselves in the centre of a deadly game of cat and mouse after taking a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride.
facts.title: Cop Car

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: What begins as an impulsive childhood joy ride quickly turns lethal once the cruiser's dangerous owner realizes it is missing.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After stumbling upon an abandoned police cruiser and taking it for a reckless joy ride, two kids trigger a deadly, high-stakes game of cat and mouse with a ruthless sheriff in director Jon Watts's compact crime thriller.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: A fast, taut crime thriller that delivers sharp suspense and engaged focus without unnecessary weight.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Clocking in at a lean 88 minutes, this fast, suspenseful pursuit strips the thriller formula down to its bare essentials with unrelenting momentum and constant tension.

issueSummaries: description: 'stumbling upon an abandoned police cruiser' asserts a specific acquisition circumstance (the cruiser was unattended/abandoned) that is not established by allowedSourceMaterial.overview, which only says the kids took 'a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride' without specifying whether the vehicle was abandoned or its owner was nearby.

description: 'ruthless sheriff' attributes a specific character trait/personality to the sheriff that is not supported by allowedSourceMaterial.overview, which contains no characterization of the sheriff beyond ownership of the cruiser.
curiosityHook: 'the cruiser's dangerous owner' similarly invents a character trait ('dangerous') for the sheriff that is not established by the authorized overview.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Per A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1, unsupported additions require intervention when they materially specify factual attributes or identity/relationship traits not established by the authorized packet. 'Abandoned' concretizes an unstated circumstance of the cruiser's acquisition, and 'ruthless'/'dangerous' attribute unestablished character traits to the sheriff. These are bounded, fixable overstatements — not inventions of plot mechanics, causality, or spoiler-boundary material — so MINOR is appropriate rather than SEVERE. Excluding facts.keywords from authorization (per prior guidance) means these traits cannot be grounded even though 'corrupt sheriff' appears there.

sourceEvidence.notes: Overview supports: two kids take a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride and become the center of a deadly cat-and-mouse game. This grounds the premise, initial conflict, and general tone of description, curiosityHook, and vibeSummary.

The overview does not state that the cruiser was abandoned or unattended; 'taking a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride' is compatible with multiple acquisition scenarios, so specifying 'abandoned' is an unsupported concretization of circumstance.
No personality/character trait for the sheriff (e.g., 'ruthless', 'dangerous') is established by the overview. The overview identifies the sheriff only via possession of the cruiser.

whyWatch's '88 minutes' matches facts.runtimeMinutes exactly; description's attribution to director Jon Watts and framing as a 'crime thriller' align with facts.director and facts.genres (Crime, Thriller).
vibeSummary's 'fast, taut... sharp suspense and engaged focus' directly reflects the authorized pace (fast), moods (suspenseful), and attentionDemand (engaged) classifications.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: If facts.keywords were treated as part of the authorized source (contra the prior instruction to disregard them), 'corrupt sheriff' could arguably support a 'dangerous'/'ruthless' characterization; under the current closed-world reading restricted to allowedSourceMaterial and core facts, this support is absent.

geminiAdvisory.claimSpan: stumbling upon an abandoned police cruiser
issueSummaries: description: 'stumbling upon an abandoned police cruiser' introduces an unsupported factual concretization regarding the inciting plot mechanics and vehicle status; the authorized overview establishes only that two kids took a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride, with no packet grounding that the car was abandoned or discovered by chance.
geminiAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1, editorial inference is permitted for genre shorthand and rhetorical framing, but unsupported additions require intervention when they falsely specify plot mechanics or factual attributes. Describing the vehicle as an 'abandoned police cruiser' that the children 'stumbled upon' concretizes the inciting theft mechanism with ungrounded external plot specifics. The remaining copy across curiosityHook, vibeSummary, and whyWatch remains fully compliant.

sourceEvidence.notes: The overview states that two kids find themselves in a deadly game of cat and mouse 'after taking a sheriff's cruiser for a joy ride', but does not state or imply that the cruiser was 'abandoned' or that they 'stumbled upon' it.
Directly verifies Jon Watts as director.
Supports experiential attributes including 'fast' pace, 'suspenseful' mood, 'engaged' attention demand, and 'moderate' emotional weight.

geminiAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: If 'abandoned' is viewed loosely as colloquial hyperbole for an unattended vehicle left momentarily accessible, an argument could be made for tolerance; however, because it concretely alters the factual condition of an in-service law enforcement vehicle and imports specific unverified plot staging, it is conservatively flagged as MINOR.
